## Natural history notes

A tiny moth fly characterized by a fuzzy gray to brown body, broad rounded wings held roof-like over the body, and pale spots along the wing margins. In Florida, the Bathroom Moth Fly is common around bathrooms, kitchens, floor drains, sinks, septic areas, wet compost, and other damp places where organic film or sludge accumulates. Adults are weak fliers and often rest on walls near drains, while the larvae feed on bacteria, algae, fungi, and decaying organic matter in wet buildup, helping break down fine organic material but sometimes becoming a nuisance indoors.
